Federated learning enables collaborative model training across multiple devices, 
yet its security is compromised by data leakage through intermediate computations. 
To address this issue, we introduce Flatee, a federated learning framework that 
utilizes trusted execution environments to safeguard computations and data. 
Flatee's design ensures that computations are performed within secure environments, 
and we demonstrate its effectiveness through a case study involving a federated 
learning model for image classification. Our evaluation reveals that Flatee achieves 
a balance between security and performance, with a 1.5x speedup over a comparable 
approach. Furthermore, Flatee's modular architecture facilitates the integration 
of various trusted execution environments, including Intel SGX and Arm TrustZone. 
Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/Secure-ML/Flatee.

This study examines the spread of COVID-19 vaccine misinformation on Twitter, 
focusing on the distinction between users who adopt and those who reject false 
information. By employing a supervised learning approach, we developed a model

Twitter and have a higher likelihood of interacting with misinformation.

among users who are less active on Twitter and have a lower likelihood of 
interacting with misinformation. These findings contribute to a deeper 
understanding of the dynamics of misinformation dissemination on social media.
